title: Grateful Dead Live at P.N.E. Coliseum on 1973-06-22
source: Souree Info: Master Soundboard Reels > PCM > PCM (14-bit) (Sony L-750ESX-HFB tape); Transfer Info: PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch Pro > Tascam DA-3000 (wav 16-bit/44.1k)> Adobe Audition 3.0 > TLH flac16; this source fixes the flaws in the three circulating Clugston sources: source ID 140868 and source ID 140892; this version includes a fix in track 11, Jack Straw

ai_review.summary: Matrix‑style composite with generally good sound (some static) captures a marathon ’73 show highlighted by a monster Truckin'>The Other One>Sugar Magnolia sequence and standout China Cat Sunflower.
ai_review.review: The recording blends audience, monitor and Betty Board sources into a matrix that is mostly clear but suffers from occasional left‑channel static and balance issues on tracks like “Bertha.” Musically the show is uneven – a slower first set with sparse moments – but erupts in a spectacular second half featuring a smoking Truckin'>The Other One>Sugar Magnolia marathon, killer “China Cat Sunflower,” and tight “Playing in the Band” jam. Overall listeners love the depth of material despite the technical quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Weighted average of show quality (≈3.8) and recording quality (≈3.2) from three detailed reviews; mixed comments produce a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Composite of audience, monitor and Betty Board sources; occasional static/distortion in left channel, poor balance on “Bertha,” but overall clear with a sublime recent transfer.

standout_songs: Truckin' > The Other One > Sugar Magnolia
show_quality.setlist_flow: Two‑hour marathon; first set uneven with some low‑energy moments, second set builds into a massive jam suite culminating in an epic Truckin' > The Other One > Sugar Magnolia sequence.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Careful not to step on Bob during jams; pistons throughout “Big River,” starts GDtRFB riff in A, drives the second‑set improvisations.
band_member_comments.Phil: Shows his new split‑channel pickup ability; vocal flubs on “Here Comes Sunshine”; engages in a fierce battle with Billy later in the set.
band_member_comments.Bob: Delivers a unique jam on “China Cat Sunflower,” strong guitar work throughout, especially on the Sugar Magnolia climax.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith excels on “Race Is On,” provides brilliant step‑into signature and overall solid keyboard textures.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy’s ride/hi‑hat is loud early; one drummer works better here, notable slow‑down section in “Playing in the Band”; occasional balance issues affect drum presence.
